def parse_date(date_str):
    formats = ["%Y-%m-%d", "%d/%m/%Y", "%b %d %Y"]
    for fmt in formats:
        try:
            return datetime.strptime(date_str.strip(), fmt).date()
        except:
            pass
    raise ValueError(f"Unable to parse: {date_str}")

def to_usd(amount_str):
    amount_str = amount_str.strip()
    if "EUR" in amount_str:
        amount_str = amount_str.replace("EUR", "").strip()
        amount_str = amount_str.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
        return float(amount_str) * 1.052
    else:
        amount_str = amount_str.replace("$", "").replace(",", "")
        return float(amount_str)

# Build dictionary with last occurrence of each ID
trans_dict = {}
for line in transactions_raw.strip().split('\n'):
    parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split('|')]
    tid, date_str, region, customer, amount, status = parts
    trans_dict[tid] = (date_str, amount, status)

# Filter for date range and paid status
start = datetime.strptime("2024-05-31", "%Y-%m-%d").date()
end = datetime.strptime("2024-07-26", "%Y-%m-%d").date()

paid_statuses = {"paid", "PAID", "settled"}
filtered = []

for tid, (date_str, amount_str, status) in trans_dict.items():
    date = parse_date(date_str)
    if start <= date <= end and status.lower() in paid_statuses:
        amount_usd = to_usd(amount_str)
        filtered.append((tid, date, amount_usd))
